axes.model_access: Multi-provider aggregation: Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google/Vertex AI, the OpenAI Responses API, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint and Ollama. Models and keys are configured by the deployer and can be switched inside a conversation; check the official Features page for the current provider list.
axes.runtime: Self-hosted web app: Docker Compose (with MongoDB, MeiliSearch and a RAG API) or a manual npm deployment; one-click Railway deployment is also offered. Data and inference credentials stay on your server and do not pass through LibreChat’s cloud.
axes.local_files: Attachment upload, RAG API document retrieval and a Code Interpreter sandbox. Files and vector indexes live in your MongoDB or storage, and the sandbox is yours to deploy; isolation depends on the runtime configuration.
axes.background: Scheduled Chats can create a new conversation and run a prompt on a schedule; Code Interpreter and agent tasks run server-side. Whether they survive shutdown depends on whether the instance and sandbox stay running.
axes.tools: MCP servers, OpenAPI Actions, Agents, Skills, Subagents, Agent Plugins and Code Interpreter; tool approval and Tool Search are configured in the agent instructions.
axes.context: The context window is set by the connected model. Conversation history, Message Search, User Memory and agent-owned context are managed separately; cross-project memory boundaries follow the official Memory documentation.
axes.permissions: Multi-user auth (OAuth2, LDAP, email), roles and groups, Admin Panel, rate limits, automated moderation and token spend statistics; enterprise SSO and fine-grained permissions depend on the deployment.
axes.fit: Fits: teams that want a self-hosted, multi-model chat platform with agents, MCP and RAG, and can operate MongoDB, MeiliSearch and a sandbox. Does not fit: a single-model lightweight front end, or teams unwilling to maintain a database.
